# How to Create AI Cooking Videos That Get Views on Social Media

Cooking channels live or die by posting cadence, and editing every recipe by hand kills momentum. The practical question is which AI tools auto-cut, caption, and resize your cooking footage into scroll-stopping clips

## The decision before you

Decide what "finished" looks like for you before comparing anything. 9 of the tools below have a free or freemium tier, so budget is rarely what decides this — your skill level and the kind of content you ship matter more. Nothing here needs a card to try. Each entry below states what it is good at and where it stops, so match one to a task you do repeatedly

## The tools worth considering

### VEED.io

[[link:/tools/51|VEED.io]] is a Freemium video tool for Beginners, Social Media, Marketing. It handles social Media Reels and Course Video Editing, and its key strength is that no software to install — everything runs in the browser with automatic cloud saving. The honest limit: browser-based means performance depends on internet speed and browser capabilities

### AI Video Editor

[[link:/tools/612|AI Video Editor]] is a Freemium video tool for Video Editing, Content Creation, YouTube. It handles automated Cuts and Scene Detection, and its key strength is that automation handles repetitive editing work for solo creators. The honest limit: automated cuts may not match a specific creative vision

### Fliki

[[link:/tools/278|Fliki]] is a Freemium video tool for Text-to-Video, AI Voices, Marketing. It handles blog-to-Video and Social Snippets, and its key strength is that text-to-video workflow needs no filming or editing experience. The honest limit: stock-visual matching can feel generic on niche topics

### InShot AI

[[link:/tools/1478|InShot AI]] is a Freemium video tool for Mobile, Reels, TikTok. It handles reel Editing and Auto Captions, and its key strength is that mobile-first workflow lets creators shoot and edit anywhere. The honest limit: phone-based editing struggles with longer or complex projects

### ElevenLabs

[[link:/tools/8|ElevenLabs]] is a Freemium audio tool for Professionals, High Quality, Content Creation. It handles audiobook Narration and Game Character Voices, and its key strength is that voice quality and emotional range are among the best available today. The honest limit: free tier is limited; serious production requires a paid plan

### Murf AI

[[link:/tools/78|Murf AI]] is a Freemium audio tool for Content Creation, Beginners, Quick Results. It handles corporate Training Videos and Podcast Intros & Outros, and its key strength is that 120+ voices with granular control over pitch, speed, pause, and emphasis — studio-grade output. The honest limit: free plan limited to 10 minutes of voice generation — not enough for serious projects

### CapCut Pro AI

[[link:/tools/1512|CapCut Pro AI]] is a Freemium video tool for Video Editing, Short Video, Social Media. It handles auto Subtitles and One-Click Templates, and its key strength is that automatic subtitles remove tedious manual captioning work from editing. The honest limit: templates can make videos look similar across creators

### Opus Clip

[[link:/tools/1534|Opus Clip]] is a Freemium video tool for Content Creators, Podcasters, YouTubers. It handles podcast Clips and YouTube Repurposing, and its key strength is that automates clip selection from hours of long-form footage. The honest limit: automatic selections can miss important context-heavy discussion moments

### CapCut

[[link:/tools/1512|CapCut]] is a Freemium video tool for Short-Form Video, Auto Captions, Social Media. It handles auto Captions and Background Removal, and its key strength is that core editing features are free on desktop and mobile. The honest limit: some advanced effects and features sit behind the paid tier

## How to choose

Start where the friction is highest. If you are unsure, begin with [[link:/tools/612|AI Video Editor]] and [[link:/tools/51|VEED.io]], since both handle routine work and neither demands much setup. Add a specialist later, and only for a task you have already done often enough to know it needs one. Pay only after a free tier has demonstrably run out on work you actually do

## A workflow you can chain today

Record the cook once, auto-edit in [[link:/tools/612|AI Video Editor]], add captions and trims in [[link:/tools/51|VEED.io]], voice steps with [[link:/tools/78|Murf AI]], then export vertical versions via [[link:/tools/1478|InShot AI]]

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Treating AI output as final. Drafts, voice and clips still need a human pass for accuracy, tone and brand fit.
- Ignoring skill level. Some of these are usable immediately; a few expect you to configure them first, and that mismatch costs afternoons.
- Stacking too many subscriptions. Several options here are paid, so trial the free tiers before committing monthly.
- Skipping verification. Generated content invents specifics with confidence, and they are not always true

## FAQ

### What is the fastest way to edit cooking footage?

[[link:/tools/612|AI Video Editor]] detects scenes and [[link:/tools/1512|CapCut Pro AI]] adds auto subtitles, cutting manual work

### Do I need a separate voice tool?

[[link:/tools/78|Murf AI]] or [[link:/tools/8|ElevenLabs]] can narrate steps if your video is silent

### Which format performs best?

Vertical clips via [[link:/tools/1478|InShot AI]] and [[link:/tools/1512|CapCut]] suit Reels and Shorts

### How do I keep recipes accurate?

Always write the ingredient list yourself; use AI only for editing and pacing

## Final takeaway

One tool per stage, reviewed by you, beats one tool trying to do everything. Try the two or three that match what you actually do, and add more only when a repeated task demands it.
tldr: Record once, auto-edit with one tool, then export vertical versions for each platform.
